purpose: Derive CACHE_SIZE_WARN_CHUNKS from data instead of inheriting it from a deleted design.

hardware.gpu: Intel Arc 140V (Xe2) — not used by this measurement

methodology.what_is_measured: wall-clock of a single retrieve(query, k=4) call
methodology.cache_population: retrieval caches (_chunk_vecs, _chunk_texts, _fts) written directly rather than via approve(), because per-chunk AES cost is not under test and would cap reachable N
methodology.queries: 8 fixed queries cycled; 2 warm-up calls discarded
methodology.box_state: quiet — no model loaded, assistant down, archive download PAUSED for the duration

derived.threshold_rationale: the measured row below the 100 ms crossing (79 ms), leaving headroom to act before the cost is felt

not_measured: cost with REAL embeddings and real text lengths (random vectors and 24-word texts were used)
cost under concurrent load or with the model resident on the same box
the encrypt/decrypt cost of growing the store to these sizes via approve()
memory footprint at each size — only latency was timed
whether SQLite FTS5 BM25 cost scales differently with realistic term-frequency distributions than with the uniform random vocabulary used here
